fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Why data is the devil's tool here", "body": "Beth opened with Art Zimmerman's line that God knows everything and the devil wants to know everything, and asked why the beast is so hungry for our data. Chance said that in individual experience the tension between good and evil teaches us what is right, but that big tech uses data differently, as control. He argued that data-driven decisions would train people out of deciding for themselves while leaving them convinced the choices were their own. He tied it to his earlier appearances on Gnosticism and simulation theory."}, {"title": "Numbers, samples and shaky statistics", "body": "Asked what birthed the data beast, Chance pointed to the moment numbers lost their spiritual meaning and became abstract integers, which he called a Luciferian fall that lets people be seen as statistics. He questioned how a sample of 300 can speak for 350 million people and described the replication crisis in published studies. He argued that studies often begin with a conclusion, create an illusion of causality, and that larger data harvesting only gives the harvesters sharper predictions. Beth added the point about studies built to prove what is already assumed."}, {"title": "Cybernetics and closed feedback loops", "body": "Beth read James Corbett's 2017 editorial Big Data Exposed, which covered psychographic profiling, Cambridge Analytica and the marionette image from Pinocchio. Chance then explained cybernetics, learned from Wayne McRoy Jr, as systems control over living things and machines alike. He contrasted the body's distributed feedback loops with closed loops such as addiction, and said social media memes and single-source communities work the same way. He showed a weighted tuning fork on reflexology points as an example of using an internal loop in a positive way."}, {"title": "The leaked Google video and the barcode", "body": "Beth played a leaked internal Google video that described user data as a ledger in the Lamarckian sense, passed across generations and used to nudge behavior toward chosen goals. Chance said it showed that the corporate world plans generations ahead while the public debates smartphones. He questioned genetics as a mechanistic code and linked DNA to the twin serpents of the caduceus. He then pulled up the International Barcode of Life website, noting its serpent logo and its stated aim to illuminate biodiversity, and argued that life cannot be catalogued by dissection."}, {"title": "Middlemen, containers and counting", "body": "Chance argued that the devil figure in these systems is the middleman, linking Mercury, the messenger of the gods, to commerce, banking and the Hermes name he noticed in PayPal's web addresses. He said attention is spiritual currency and recommended building one's own containers such as a website. He read about Palantir and Pegasus spyware, then discussed counting. He said numbers are abstractions, resources are really source, and keeping score in relationships turns them into a game. Beth responded with her thoughts on accountants and the Count Dracula image."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Beth Martens had me back on King Hero's Journey for the third time, and we took on big data as a system of control. We watched a leaked Google video, Beth read James Corbett, and I read up on Palantir and waved around a weighted tuning fork. It ran two hours, and the counting segment at the end is a fun one.
